     The lung and chest wall are two distensible bodies, whose com pliances are essential for the
      respiratory function. We  will discuss som e essential mechanical properties  of an elastic
      balloon, before elaborating on com pliances of lung and chest wall.


     A. Comp lian ce of a balloon
     As shown in the  fi gure, a balloon can be infl ated in two ways. Ei ther a vol um e dV is injected
       into the balloon increasing inside pressure (Pi), or the vol um e dV is removed from the inside of
     non com pressible box decreasing  outside pressure  of the  balloon (Po).  In  both cases
     expansion of the balloon with vol um e dV is associ ated with a positive transm ural pressure
      difference (Pi – Po ) independent of whether inside pressure is increased or outside pressure is
     decreased. This transm ural pressure difference (Ptm)  is the distending pressure  for  the
      balloon and  infl ates the balloon by vol um e dV.  If the experiment is repeated with different
       vol um es, and all vol um es are plotted against their corresponding Ptm val ues, we obtain the
      relationship between vol um e and distending pressure of the balloon, and the curve displ aying
       this  relationship  is  cal led Volume/Ptm curve (see above   fi gure). The slope  of  this curve
      represents compliance, which is defined as changes in vol um e (dV) divided by changes in
     transm ural pressure difference (dPtm ). If a small change in distending pressure, Ptm, causes a
      large change in vol um e, the balloon is obviously more com pliant. Pl ease consider that the
      slope of this V/Ptm curve and thus com pliance of the balloon is not constant and depends on
      the vol um e of the balloon. The higher the balloon vol um e the lower is its com pliance.
